chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd from Uthman ibn Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who returns from a journey after Asr prayer in the month of Ramadan, and he has intercourse with his wife when she has become pure from her menses. Is it permissible for him to have intercourse with her? He said, 'There is no harm (in it).'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Can a returning traveler have intercourse with his wife in the afternoon of Ramadan and still have a valid fast?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of marital intimacy for a traveler returning after Asr in Ramadan, ruling that intercourse is permissible and does not invalidate the fast, provided the wife is pure from menstruation. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the prohibition of intercourse during fasting applies specifically to the time before sunset, allowing travelers to resume marital relations immediately upon return if conditions are met. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the obligations of travelers (*musafir*) during the holy month.
